title: Data Model and Schema
definition: A data model selects entities, fields, relationships, constraints, and representations for a purpose; a schema makes part of that structural contract explicit and checkable.
purpose: Translate requirements into a consistent structure that producers and consumers can understand and validate.
history: Schemas appear in programming languages, file formats, databases, messages, and validation systems with different enforcement times.
mental_model: A blueprint for valid data shapes, not the data instance itself.
analogy: A form template compared with one completed form; useful while recognizing that cross-field business rules may exceed simple shape checks.
industry_notes: Static types, runtime validation, storage schema, and domain rules are complementary enforcement layers.
ai_notes: Require explicit source requirement, type, requiredness, default policy, and validation layer for each AI-proposed field.
interview_notes: Ask how schema differs from an example object and where validation should occur.
